name: C-17 gray (Air Mobility Command)
description: Overall gray, the radome and engines too. 'U.S. AIR FORCE' in dark gray capitals behind the flight deck, above the crew door. A small U.S. flag high on the fin above the command's letters and the base's tail band; the low-visibility star-and-bar on the aft fuselage behind the wing. Each jet's tail band, serial and unit badges differ, and aren't drawn.

gray.name: C-17 gray (sampled from the photos, sunlit to shade)

logos.description: A small U.S. flag high on the fin, the canton forward on both sides.
The national insignia in low-visibility gray: a star in a ring, a bar either side, outlined, behind the wing.

titles.style: Dark gray block capitals behind the flight deck.

notes: Measured off the RIAT 2017 photo of 07-7172 (left side), anchored at the nose tip and the tail cone: the title 0.080-0.193 along, its caps from y 0.16 to 0.30; the insignia centred 0.729 along; the flag a third back on the fin's chord at half its height. The gray is a midtone of the photo's sunlit (#ACBAC2) and shaded (#526269) sides. Air Mobility Command's jets; other services' and nations' C-17s (the RAF's, RCAF's, RAAF's, India's, Qatar's, NATO's) are gray too with their own markings, and aren't this scheme.
